results.title: Fake countdown timer
results.question: Does the "sale ends in…" timer restart when you reload?
results.finding: The timer showed 14:17, then 14:54 after waiting 10s and reloading. It restarted, so the deadline isn't real.
results.fix: Count the countdown down to a real, fixed end date stored on the server. It must never restart on reload.

kane.summary:
You asked to find the sale countdown timer, wait 10 seconds, and reload the page.
A countdown timer was found in the Black Friday Megasale banner and recorded as 14:17.
After waiting and reloading the cart page, the timer was recorded as 14:54.
No payment details were entered and no order was placed.

results.objective: Go to http://localhost:8080/. Look for a sale countdown timer on the page (for example "Sale ends in 14:59"). Store the exact time it shows as timer_first. Wait 10 seconds, then reload the page. Store the exact time the same countdown shows right after the reload as timer_after_reload. If the page has no countdown timer, store "none" as timer_first and "none" as timer_after_reload. Never enter payment details and never place a real order.

results.title: Fake "only N left" stock
results.question: Does the scarcity message change on every reload?
results.finding: Nobody bought anything, but the stock count changed between reloads: 3 → 5 → 5. The scarcity is made up.
results.fix: Show the real inventory number from your database, or drop the scarcity message.

kane.summary:
You asked to record the first product’s name and its stock or scarcity message, then check that message again after two page reloads.
The first product was identified as AirWave Pro Earbuds.
Its initial stock message was “🔥 Only 3 left — 23 people viewing!”.
After the first reload, the stock message was “🔥 Only 5 left — 23 people viewing!”.
After the second reload, the stock message remained “🔥 Only 5 left — 23 people viewing!”.
No items were added to the cart, and no order or payment action was taken.

results.objective: Go to http://localhost:8080/. Find a stock or scarcity message on the first product (for example "Only 3 left" or "12 in stock") and store its exact text as stock_1. Reload the page and store the same product's stock message as stock_2. Reload once more and store it as stock_3. Do not add anything to the cart. If there is no stock message, store "none" for all three. Never enter payment details and never place a real order.

results.title: Sneaky add-on in cart
results.question: Does something you didn’t choose end up in your cart?
results.finding: Added only "AirWave Pro Earbuds", but the cart had 2 items: ShieldPlus Protection Plan was added without asking.
results.fix: Never add extras (protection plans, insurance, donations) by default. Offer them as an unticked option.

stored.cart_items: AirWave Pro Earbuds | ShieldPlus Protection Plan

kane.summary:
Opened the first product, AirWave Pro Earbuds.
Added the product to the cart without selecting any additional options, then opened the cart.
The cart showed 2 line items: AirWave Pro Earbuds and ShieldPlus Protection Plan.
No payment details were entered and no order was placed.

results.objective: Go to http://localhost:8080/. Open the first product. Store its name as product_name. Click "Add to cart" without ticking or choosing any extra options. Then open the cart. Store the names of every line item in the cart, separated by " | ", as cart_items, and store how many different line items are in the cart as cart_line_count. Never enter payment details and never place a real order.

results.title: Hidden fees at checkout
results.question: Does the final total match the price you were shown?
results.finding: Listed at $49.00, but the final total was $56.49 (+$7.49: Service & handling). The extra cost only appeared on the last step.
results.fix: Show every mandatory fee in the price on the product page. No surprise charges at the final step.

kane.summary:
Opened the first product, AirWave Pro Earbuds, and recorded its listed price as $49.00.
Added the product to the cart without extras; an additional ShieldPlus Protection Plan was found in the cart and removed.
Continued through checkout using simple test information and reached the final order review page.
Stopped at the review page without entering payment details or placing an order.
The review page showed a final total of $56.49, including a Service & handling fee.

results.objective: Go to http://localhost:8080/. Open the first product and store its displayed price as listed_price. Add it to the cart without any extras. If the cart contains anything else you did not add, remove it. Go to checkout and continue until the final order review page, filling any required fields with simple test text. Do not enter payment details and do not place the order. Store the final order total shown on the review page as final_total, and store the names of any fees added on top of the product price as extra_fees (or "none"). Never enter payment details and never place a real order.

results.title: Hard-to-cancel subscription
results.question: Is cancelling much harder than joining?
results.fix: Make cancelling as easy as joining: one clearly labelled "Cancel membership" button and one confirmation. No guilt-trip wording, no required survey.

kane.summary:
You asked to find and join the store’s membership or subscription, then cancel it without entering payment details or placing an order.
A membership option was found and joined; no form was required.
The membership was then cancelled successfully, and the site reached its cancellation confirmation page.
Joining required 3 clicks, pages, or forms; cancellation required 16.
No guilt-inducing button or message was shown during cancellation.

results.objective: Go to http://localhost:8080/. Find the store's membership or subscription and join it. Count every click, page and form you needed until you were a member, and store that number as join_steps. Then cancel the membership. Count every click, page and form needed until the site confirms it is cancelled, and store that number as cancel_steps. If a form is required, fill it with simple test text. If any button guilt-trips you for leaving (for example "No, I hate saving money"), store its exact text as guilt_text, otherwise store "none". If there is no membership or subscription, store "none" as join_steps and cancel_steps. Never enter payment details and never place a real order.
